## What's new

- **Orca as a second runner.** Worktrees, multirepo groups and the multirepo agent open in [Orca](https://www.onorca.dev) with their environment and agent, and Orca's `orca.yaml` scripts can prepare and release its own worktrees with `shogun`. The control tower shows the state Orca reports for each agent, the tool it's waiting on, its prompt and its last message, and the ports each worktree listens on.
- **Choose your default runner.** Pick Herdr or Orca in Preferences: "Open", the menu bar, the Worktree menu, its shortcut, the guided tour and the instructions agents read all follow it.
- **Orca's board kept in step.** Each worktree's status, a summary and its GitHub pull request or issue appear on Orca's board without moving them by hand.
- **Devices in Orca's emulator view.** A worktree's Android emulator or iOS simulator shows up in Orca's emulator view when it starts or when the worktree opens in Orca.
- **Desktop turn in Orca.** Claude takes the desktop turn by itself before Orca's computer use acts, so two agents never drive the screen at once.
- **A redesigned app.** New colours where red only means danger, compact forms and dialogs, one consistent row and detail layout, a status bar with the machine's resources, and every worktree action available in the same places: detail, context menu, command palette, menu bar and Worktree menu.
- **Release notes inside the app.** When a new version is out, click the ⓘ icon on the update notice or "What's new" to read what it brings, in your language, without leaving ShogunAi. If you skipped a few versions, you see the notes of each one, newest first, and "View on GitHub" opens the release page.
- **Flutter repositories.** Every new worktree gets `flutter pub get`, and its Android build is handled by the Gradle and emulator providers.
- **CocoaPods without waiting.** New worktrees get the base repository's pods cloned instantly when the lock files match, and the DerivedData view shows how much of it are Swift packages, next to the shared SwiftPM and CocoaPods caches.
- **Idle Maven daemons.** Maven daemons now show whether they're busy or idle and the idle ones can be stopped, as Gradle's already could.
- **Merged into its base.** A branch created from an epic or another branch counts as merged as soon as it's merged into that base, not only into the main branch, and `shogun new` remembers which branch a worktree started from.
- **Multirepo settings from the command line.** Shared variables and the workspace repository of a multirepo can be edited with `shogun multirepo` instead of by hand.

## Fixes

- **Opening the app from the Dock.** A `shogun` command installed with Homebrew is no longer reported as missing from the `PATH`, and the guided tour starts.
- **Local files checked before creating a worktree.** If a file to copy or link is missing or can't be read, ShogunAi says which one, where it looked and how to fix it before creating anything, instead of failing half-way.
- **Signed and notarized on macOS.** The `.dmg` is signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it without the "developer cannot be verified" warning.
- **Claude Code hooks in Preferences.** The hooks' Install and Remove buttons now sit under the Claude Code section, not next to the command-line tool.
